questions.q: What problem do reference data sets solve?
options: They let different business units use different values for the same kind of setup data, like payment terms
They assign currencies to legal entities
They replace the need for a chart of accounts
They control journal approval limits only
questions.explain: Reference data sets let different business units see different values for the same type of reference data, such as payment terms, without needing separate application instances.

questions.q: What is a reference data set?
options: A single transaction record
A named grouping of reference data values that a business unit can be assigned to
A type of chart of accounts value set
A conversion rate type
questions.explain: A reference data set is a named grouping of values for a partitioned reference data type, assigned to one or more business units.

questions.q: What is the Common Set (Enterprise Set) used for?
options: A set reserved exclusively for secondary ledgers
A set that cannot be assigned to any business unit
Reference data that should be visible to every business unit regardless of other set assignments
Data only legal entities can see
questions.explain: The Common Set holds reference data meant to be shared across every business unit, avoiding unnecessary duplication when values don't actually vary.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is a downside of over-segmenting reference data into many named sets when the Common Set would do?
options: It automatically breaks the chart of accounts
It prevents any business unit from processing transactions
There is no downside; more sets are always better
It adds unnecessary ongoing maintenance
questions.explain: Creating more reference data sets than necessary adds maintenance burden without providing real value when the data doesn't actually need to vary by business unit.

questions.q: What is a 'determinant,' as previewed in this lesson?
options: A chart of accounts segment qualifier
A value from the transaction's context, usually the business unit, used to identify which reference data set applies
A type of accounting calendar
A legal entity's registered address
questions.explain: A determinant, most commonly the business unit, is the contextual value Oracle Fusion uses to decide which reference data set should apply to a given transaction.
